segments.text: Welcome to part seven. This is the habit
that separates a smooth AI setup from a
nightmare. Every project gets its own
virtual environment. Let me show you why
and how.
Imagine project A needs one version of a
library
>> [music]
>> and project B needs a newer one. If you
install everything into the one global
Python, the second install breaks the
first project. AI libraries are the
worst for this because they depend on
exact versions of each other. A virtual
environment is a private folder with its
own Python and its own libraries for one
project only. This is built into Python.
The official documentation calls it the
venv module and this is the real page.
In your project folder, type python -m
venv space .venv.
>> [music]
>> The last part is the folder name and
.venv is the standard choice. It takes
about 20 seconds because it copies a
fresh Python.
Now activate it. .\
.venv\scripts\activate.ps1.
Look at the prompt. It now starts with
.venv in brackets. That is your signal
that you're inside the environment. If
PowerShell refuses to run the script,
the fix is on a Microsoft page linked in
the description about execution policy.
On my PC, it just works.
Let me prove which Python is running.
This prints the environment folder
inside my project. Good. From now on,
Python and pip only touch this folder.
First, update pip itself.
>> [music]
>> A new environment comes with an older
pip, which is why you saw that notice.
>> [snorts]
>> python -m pip install library.
numpy is the base of numerical Python
and the first library of every AI stack.
It installs number py 2.5.4.
Pip list shows exactly what is in this
environment. Number py and pip. Nothing
else, so it is clean.
Now, the sharing trick. Pip freeze
greater than requirements.txt
saves the exact versions into a text
file. Here's the file. A friend, a
server, or you in 6 months can recreate
the same environment with one command.
Pip install-r requirements.txt.
Commit this file to get from part six.
To leave the environment, type
deactivate. The prompt goes back to
normal. To delete an environment, just
delete its folder. You never lose
anything because requirements.txt
can rebuild it.
One more tool you'll see everywhere in
AI projects, uv. It is a very fast
Python package installer from a company
called Astral. This is its official
installation page. There are several
ways to install it. I use pip with
python-m pip install uv.
I run uv as python-m
uv because on my PC the plain uv command
is not on the path after user install.
>> [music]
>> It is version 0.13.5.
Then uv venv creates an environment.
[music] And uv pip install puts pandas,
the data library, into [music] it. Watch
the speed. Five packages prepared in 3
and 1/2 seconds and installed in under
two. That is why many AI teams use uv.
>> [music]
>> Everything we do in this masterclass
works with plain pip or with uv, your
choice.
Your environments are ready. Next, part
eight, Jupyter notebooks, the tool
behind most AI tutorials. Like, share
and subscribe, and see you there.
